title: Thymosin-ɑ1 for people with chronic hepatitis B.
abstract: RATIONALE: Chronic hepatitis B is a global public health concern. It is caused by infection with the hepatitis B virus (HBV). The goal of treating chronic HBV infection is to prevent progression to chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, liver failure, hepatocellular carcinoma, and death. Individual studies have evaluated various immunomodulatory therapies with inconsistent results. Thymosin-ɑ1 is known to have antiviral effects; however, results of randomised clinical trials on the effects of thymosin-α1 as a potential treatment for people with chronic HBV have been inconsistent. OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of thymosin-ɑ1 therapy in people with chronic hepatitis B. SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group Controlled Trials Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, four other databases and six trials registers, in addition to reference checking, citation searching, and contacting study authors to identify trials for inclusion. The latest search date was 10 June 2026. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated thymosin-α1 at any dose, route of administration, or formulation type, in people with chronic hepatitis B regardless of age, sex, or ethnicity. Thymosin-α1 could have been administered as monotherapy, in combination with an additional drug, or in addition to standard medical treatment and compared with placebo, no intervention, the same additional drug, or the same standard medical treatment. OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, and health-related quality of life. Among our important outcomes were HBV-related morbidity, HBV-related mortality, non-serious adverse events, and the proportion of people without histological improvements. RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane Risk of bias 2 tool (RoB 2) to assess risk of bias. SYNTHESIS METHODS: We followed Cochrane methods. We conducted meta-analyses for predefined outcomes using data from the longest follow-up period, irrespective of the risk of bias judgements. We presented dichotomous outcome results as risk ratios (RRs) and continuous outcome results as mean differences, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) at their longest follow-ups. We used the random-effects model for our primary analyses. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence for each outcome. INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 10 RCTs conducted in Bangladesh, China, Italy, Korea, Singapore, and Taiwan, with 1349 randomised participants (range: 12 to 690; 1045 (77.5%) were male). Among the trials reporting age, none included participants younger than 17 years (age range: 17 to 75 years). The trials were published between 1991 and 2018, and assessed thymosin-ɑ1 in adults with chronic hepatitis B infection, with or without comorbidities. Only two trials mentioned comorbidities (cirrhosis and acute-on-chronic liver failure). The trials compared thymosin-ɑ1, with or without a cointervention, with placebo or no intervention, or with the same cointervention. The control interventions were placebos in two trials and no intervention in two. The remaining six trials administered co-interventions, such as interferon, pegylated interferon, lamivudine, and standard medical therapy (entecavir or tenofovir), and entecavir. Follow-ups ranged from six months to five years after the end of treatment (median: 12 months). Four trials were funded by industry, five by research grants, and one provided no information. All 10 trials (11 records) provided data on at least one outcome in our review. We identified no ongoing trials. Sixteen studies are awaiting assessment due to incomplete reporting. We received no responses to our enquiries. SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Thymosin-ɑ1, compared with the control interventions, may reduce all-cause mortality (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 907 participants; very low-certainty evidence), serious adverse events (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.99; I2 = 0%; 5 studies, 1056 participants; low-certainty evidence), HBV-related mortality (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 907 participants; very low-certainty evidence), non-serious adverse events (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.83; I2 = 0%; 5 studies, 300 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and may have little to no effect on health-related quality of life (MD 0.70, 95% CI -2.55 to 3.95; I2 not applicable; 1 study, 161 participants; very low-certainty evidence; score range: 0 to 100; the higher the score, the better) and on histological improvement (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.13 to 2.06; I2 = 74%; 2 studies, 702 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of thymosin-ɑ1 on hepatitis B-related morbidity (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.40; I2 = 3%; 3 studies, 854 participants; very low-certainty evidence). We judged the certainty of evidence to be low for serious adverse events and very low for the remaining outcomes. Reasons for downgrading were mainly due to study limitations, including overall high or some concerns for risk of bias; imprecision of the pooled effect estimates (including wide or very wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect, and small participant numbers); and inconsistency due to substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 74%). The test for subgroup differences provided no evidence of differences in effect according to thymosin‐α1 administration for any outcome (P ≥ 0.05). AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: We assessed the certainty of evidence as very low for all outcomes except for serious adverse events (low). Therefore, we are not sure whether thymosin-α1 monotherapy versus placebo or no intervention, or with the same co-interventions, reduces all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, HBV-related mortality, and non-serious adverse events, nor whether it has any effect on quality of life (based on one trial) and histological improvement. The effect of thymosin-ɑ1 on HBV-related morbidity is very uncertain. We observed no statistically significant differences between trials with and without cointerventions. We found no ongoing trials. FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding. REGISTRATION: Protocol available via DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD014610.

title_zh: 胸腺素-α1用于慢性乙型肝炎患者。
source_body_en: RATIONALE: Chronic hepatitis B is a global public health concern. It is caused by infection with the hepatitis B virus (HBV). The goal of treating chronic HBV infection is to prevent progression to chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, liver failure, hepatocellular carcinoma, and death. Individual studies have evaluated various immunomodulatory therapies with inconsistent results. Thymosin-ɑ1 is known to have antiviral effects; however, results of randomised clinical trials on the effects of thymosin-α1 as a potential treatment for people with chronic HBV have been inconsistent. OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of thymosin-ɑ1 therapy in people with chronic hepatitis B. SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group Controlled Trials Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, four other databases and six trials registers, in addition to reference checking, citation searching, and contacting study authors to identify trials for inclusion. The latest search date was 10 June 2026. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated thymosin-α1 at any dose, route of administration, or formulation type, in people with chronic hepatitis B regardless of age, sex, or ethnicity. Thymosin-α1 could have been administered as monotherapy, in combination with an additional drug, or in addition to standard medical treatment and compared with placebo, no intervention, the same additional drug, or the same standard medical treatment. OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, and health-related quality of life. Among our important outcomes were HBV-related morbidity, HBV-related mortality, non-serious adverse events, and the proportion of people without histological improvements. RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane Risk of bias 2 tool (RoB 2) to assess risk of bias. SYNTHESIS METHODS: We followed Cochrane methods. We conducted meta-analyses for predefined outcomes using data from the longest follow-up period, irrespective of the risk of bias judgements. We presented dichotomous outcome results as risk ratios (RRs) and continuous outcome results as mean differences, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) at their longest follow-ups. We used the random-effects model for our primary analyses. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence for each outcome. INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 10 RCTs conducted in Bangladesh, China, Italy, Korea, Singapore, and Taiwan, with 1349 randomised participants (range: 12 to 690; 1045 (77.5%) were male). Among the trials reporting age, none included participants younger than 17 years (age range: 17 to 75 years). The trials were published between 1991 and 2018, and assessed thymosin-ɑ1 in adults with chronic hepatitis B infection, with or without comorbidities. Only two trials mentioned comorbidities (cirrhosis and acute-on-chronic liver failure). The trials compared thymosin-ɑ1, with or without a cointervention, with placebo or no intervention, or with the same cointervention. The control interventions were placebos in two trials and no intervention in two. The remaining six trials administered co-interventions, such as interferon, pegylated interferon, lamivudine, and standard medical therapy (entecavir or tenofovir), and entecavir. Follow-ups ranged from six months to five years after the end of treatment (median: 12 months). Four trials were funded by industry, five by research grants, and one provided no information. All 10 trials (11 records) provided data on at least one outcome in our review. We identified no ongoing trials. Sixteen studies are awaiting assessment due to incomplete reporting. We received no responses to our enquiries. SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Thymosin-ɑ1, compared with the control interventions, may reduce all-cause mortality (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 907 participants; very low-certainty evidence), serious adverse events (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.99; I2 = 0%; 5 studies, 1056 participants; low-certainty evidence), HBV-related mortality (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 907 participants; very low-certainty evidence), non-serious adverse events (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.83; I2 = 0%; 5 studies, 300 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and may have little to no effect on health-related quality of life (MD 0.70, 95% CI -2.55 to 3.95; I2 not applicable; 1 study, 161 participants; very low-certainty evidence; score range: 0 to 100; the higher the score, the better) and on histological improvement (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.13 to 2.06; I2 = 74%; 2 studies, 702 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of thymosin-ɑ1 on hepatitis B-related morbidity (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.40; I2 = 3%; 3 studies, 854 participants; very low-certainty evidence). We judged the certainty of evidence to be low for serious adverse events and very low for the remaining outcomes. Reasons for downgrading were mainly due to study limitations, including overall high or some concerns for risk of bias; imprecision of the pooled effect estimates (including wide or very wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect, and small participant numbers); and inconsistency due to substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 74%). The test for subgroup differences provided no evidence of differences in effect according to thymosin‐α1 administration for any outcome (P ≥ 0.05). AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: We assessed the certainty of evidence as very low for all outcomes except for serious adverse events (low). Therefore, we are not sure whether thymosin-α1 monotherapy versus placebo or no intervention, or with the same co-interventions, reduces all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, HBV-related mortality, and non-serious adverse events, nor whether it has any effect on quality of life (based on one trial) and histological improvement. The effect of thymosin-ɑ1 on HBV-related morbidity is very uncertain. We observed no statistically significant differences between trials with and without cointerventions. We found no ongoing trials. FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding. REGISTRATION: Protocol available via DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD014610.

title: Extremely low diagnostic yield of routine hepatitis B and human immunodeficiency virus screening among incarcerated adults treated for hepatitis C in Western Australia.
abstract: Abstract Routine testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is recommended prior to initiating direct‐acting antiviral (DAA) therapy for hepatitis C virus (HCV) in Australian prisons. We evaluated the diagnostic yield of HBV and HIV screening among 713 incarcerated adults commencing DAA therapy across multiple Western Australian prisons between 2017 and 2025. The cohort had a mean age of 34.8 years and was predominantly male (81%). HBV and HIV screening outcomes were available for all participants. Only one (0.14%) participant tested positive for hepatitis B surface antigen and none for HIV. A further 12% had serological evidence of past HBV exposure. These findings confirm an extremely low yield of universal pre‐treatment HBV/HIV screening in this setting. While screening remains clinically important, treatment should not be delayed while awaiting results. Parallel testing strategies may streamline care and support hepatitis C elimination efforts in custodial settings. This study represents one of the largest contemporary evaluations of HBV and HIV screening outcomes among incarcerated individuals receiving DAA therapy in Australia.

title: Sequential Precise Targeted Hepatitis B Virus Therapy: Hepatitis B Virus-Specific Small Interfering RNA Followed by Aggregation-Induced Emission-Photothermal Ablation Based on Macrophage Membrane-Coated Nanoplatform.
abstract: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) afflicts approximately 254 million people worldwide and is responsible for more than one million deaths annually. Intrahepatic persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), the episomal transcriptional template of hepatitis B virus (HBV), sustains chronic replication, blunts the efficacy of antiviral therapy, and precipitates virological relapse once treatment is discontinued. While emerging cccDNA-targeted strategies include CRISPR/Cas9-mediated cleavage and epigenetic silencing, their clinical translation is impeded by delivery inefficiency, safety concerns, and limited durability. Herein, we present a sequential nano-therapeutic platform that combines small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery using HBV-pre-activated macrophage membranes (HMs) with photothermal therapy utilizing aggregation-induced emission (AIE) agents. In the first step, HM-coated lipid nanoparticles encapsulating siRNA (siR@HM NPs) enable virus to neutralize and hepatocyte targeted delivery via surface viral receptors, achieving efficient gene silencing. At 72 h post-administration, HM-coated PLGA nanoparticles loaded with an AIE photothermal agent (TPAT@HM NPs) are introduced, facilitating near-infrared IIb fluorescence-guided 808 nm laser ablation of residual infected cells. In a cell model of chronic HBV infection, both siR@HM NPs and TPAT@HM NPs achieved targeted delivery to infected hepatocytes. Critically, sequential administration yielded superior antiviral efficacy compared with concurrent administration or either monotherapy, leading to substantial reduction in HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, cccDNA, and pgRNA levels. Biosafety assessments confirmed negligible cytotoxicity, hemolysis, and systemic toxicity. This bionic platform integrates time-programmed virus targeting, RNA interference, and photothermal ablation. The virus-preactivated membrane coating enables dual recognition of both viral particles and infected cells, offering a precise and scalable theranostic strategy for HBV and other refractory viral infections.

title_zh: 序贯精确靶向 乙型肝炎病毒 治疗:基于巨噬细胞膜涂层纳米平台的 乙型肝炎病毒 特异性小干扰 RNA,随后进行聚集诱导发射光热消融。
source_body_en: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) afflicts approximately 254 million people worldwide and is responsible for more than one million deaths annually. Intrahepatic persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), the episomal transcriptional template of hepatitis B virus (HBV), sustains chronic replication, blunts the efficacy of antiviral therapy, and precipitates virological relapse once treatment is discontinued. While emerging cccDNA-targeted strategies include CRISPR/Cas9-mediated cleavage and epigenetic silencing, their clinical translation is impeded by delivery inefficiency, safety concerns, and limited durability. Herein, we present a sequential nano-therapeutic platform that combines small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery using HBV-pre-activated macrophage membranes (HMs) with photothermal therapy utilizing aggregation-induced emission (AIE) agents. In the first step, HM-coated lipid nanoparticles encapsulating siRNA (siR@HM NPs) enable virus to neutralize and hepatocyte targeted delivery via surface viral receptors, achieving efficient gene silencing. At 72 h post-administration, HM-coated PLGA nanoparticles loaded with an AIE photothermal agent (TPAT@HM NPs) are introduced, facilitating near-infrared IIb fluorescence-guided 808 nm laser ablation of residual infected cells. In a cell model of chronic HBV infection, both siR@HM NPs and TPAT@HM NPs achieved targeted delivery to infected hepatocytes. Critically, sequential administration yielded superior antiviral efficacy compared with concurrent administration or either monotherapy, leading to substantial reduction in HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, cccDNA, and pgRNA levels. Biosafety assessments confirmed negligible cytotoxicity, hemolysis, and systemic toxicity. This bionic platform integrates time-programmed virus targeting, RNA interference, and photothermal ablation. The virus-preactivated membrane coating enables dual recognition of both viral particles and infected cells, offering a precise and scalable theranostic strategy for HBV and other refractory viral infections.

title: Complete Genome Sequencing of Occult Hepatitis B Virus in Hemodialysis Patients Reveals Subgenotype D2 and Immune Escape Mutations in Bangladesh.
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health concern, and occult HBV infection (OBI) presents significant diagnostic and clinical challenges, particularly among hemodialysis (HD) patients. This study is aimed at characterizing complete HBV genomes from maintenance HD patients with OBI in Bangladesh to elucidate genetic features, mutational patterns, and clinical implications. Serum samples from two HBsAg-negative HD patients were screened by ELISA and quantitative PCR. Viral DNA was amplified by PCR across four overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) and sequenced on the Illumina platform. Genome assembly, phylogenetic analysis, and mutational profiling were performed using reference datasets and bioinformatics tools. Antigenicity and hydrophilicity of HBsAg were predicted in silico. Both patients were anti-HBc and anti-HBs positive with high HBV DNA loads (2.29 × 10 10 and 2.53 × 10 10 copies/mL). Full-length genomes (3182 bp) were successfully sequenced and phylogenetic analysis showed both HBV genomes clustered within Genotype D, Subgenotype D2, and subtype ayw3, consistent with previously reported Bangladeshi HBV genomes. Comparative mutational analysis identified substitutions such as T1753C in the basal core promoter, C1845T in preC, and D144E within the "a" determinant of HBsAg, suggesting potential roles in vaccine escape, immune escape, and diagnostic failure. Several nonsynonymous mutations were also detected in polymerase, though none were potentially associated with antiviral resistance. Antigenicity and hydrophilicity profiles of HBsAg and its major hydrophilic region remained largely conserved. These findings demonstrate the persistence of OBI in HD patients and provide an initial indication of the need for genomic surveillance to monitor immune-escape mutations and improve HBV diagnostic strategies in endemic regions.

abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 仍然是全球主要的健康问题,隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 提出了重大的诊断和临床挑战,特别是在血液透析 (HD) 患者中。本研究旨在对孟加拉国 OBI 维持性 HD 患者的完整 HBV 基因组 进行特征分析,以阐明遗传特征、突变模式和临床意义。通过 ELISA 和定量 PCR 对两名 HBsAg 阴性 HD 患者的血清样本进行了筛查。通过 PCR 在四​​个重叠的开放阅读框 (ORF) 上扩增病毒 DNA,并在 Illumina 平台上进行测序。使用参考数据集和生物信息学工具进行 基因组 组装、系统发育分析和突变分析。通过计算机预测 HBsAg 的抗原性和亲水性。两名患者均为抗 HBc 和抗 HBs 阳性,且 HBV DNA 载量较高(2.29 × 10 10 和 2.53 × 10 10 拷贝/mL)。全长 基因组 (3182 bp) 已成功测序,系统发育分析显示 HBV 基因组 聚类在基因型 D、亚型 D2 和亚型 ayw3 内,与之前报道的孟加拉国 HBV 基因组 一致。比较突变分析确定了诸如基础核心启动子中的 T1753C、preC 中的 C1845T 以及 HBsAg“a”决定簇中的 D144E 等替换,表明在 疫苗 逃逸、免疫逃逸和诊断失败中具有潜在作用。在聚合酶中也检测到了几个非同义的 突变,但没有一个与 抗病毒药物 抗性潜在相关。HBsAg 及其主要亲水区域的抗原性和亲水性特征在很大程度上保持保守。这些发现证明了 HD 患者中 OBI 的持续存在,并初步表明需要 基因组监测 来监测免疫逃逸 突变 并改进流行地区的 HBV 诊断策略。

title: Mathematical modeling of HBV-HDV transmission with superinfection: The role of vaccination and liver transplantation in disease dynamics.
abstract: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection can substantially worsen the clinical outcomes of individuals infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV), making the prevention of HBV infection and the management of severe HBV–HDV cases important public-health priorities. This study introduces a novel mathematical model for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and D virus (HDV) transmission, incorporating vaccination and liver transplantation as disease control strategies. In contrast to models that allow direct HDV infection or general coinfection pathways, the proposed model assumes that HDV occurs only through superinfection among individuals already infected with HBV. The model is constructed as a system of ordinary differential equations, where the human population is divided into susceptible, vaccinated, HBV-infected, recovered, chronic, and HDV-infected compartments. Model analysis reveals the existence and stability of the disease-free equilibrium, which exists and is asymptotically stable if the basic reproduction number ( R 0 ) is less than one, and becomes unstable if it exceeds one. Two types of endemic equilibria are identified when R 0 > 1 , corresponding to the absence and presence of HDV infection. Continuation analysis using MatCont reveals the existence of two branching points that govern the transition of stability between these equilibria, highlighting the conditions under which HDV emerges and persists. Global sensitivity analysis using Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient combined with Latin Hypercube Sampling indicates that vaccination coverage and vaccine efficacy play a dominant role in reducing R 0 . Although liver transplantation does not affect the magnitude of R 0 , it significantly influences the disease dynamics by reducing the outbreak size and delaying the timing of HBV and HDV outbreaks. These findings indicate that vaccination is essential for reducing transmission, whereas liver transplantation remains important for mitigating severe disease burden; thus, coordinated use of preventive and clinical interventions is needed for effective HBV–HDV control.

The model incorporates vaccination and liver transplantation as key interventions. It identifies the disease-free equilibrium and two types of endemic equilibria based on the basic reproduction number (R0). The analysis shows that vaccination coverage and efficacy are critical in reducing R0, while liver transplantation affects outbreak size and timing. The findings emphasize the importance of combining preventive and clinical strategies for effective HBV–HDV control. The study's results are grounded in mathematical modeling and sensitivity analysis, providing insights into disease dynamics and intervention effectiveness. However, the model's assumptions and the lack of empirical data limit the strength of the conclusions.

title_zh: 具有重复感染的 HBV-HDV 传播 的数学模型:疫苗接种 和肝移植在疾病动态中的作用。
source_body_en: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection can substantially worsen the clinical outcomes of individuals infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV), making the prevention of HBV infection and the management of severe HBV–HDV cases important public-health priorities. This study introduces a novel mathematical model for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and D virus (HDV) transmission, incorporating vaccination and liver transplantation as disease control strategies. In contrast to models that allow direct HDV infection or general coinfection pathways, the proposed model assumes that HDV occurs only through superinfection among individuals already infected with HBV. The model is constructed as a system of ordinary differential equations, where the human population is divided into susceptible, vaccinated, HBV-infected, recovered, chronic, and HDV-infected compartments. Model analysis reveals the existence and stability of the disease-free equilibrium, which exists and is asymptotically stable if the basic reproduction number ( R 0 ) is less than one, and becomes unstable if it exceeds one. Two types of endemic equilibria are identified when R 0 > 1 , corresponding to the absence and presence of HDV infection. Continuation analysis using MatCont reveals the existence of two branching points that govern the transition of stability between these equilibria, highlighting the conditions under which HDV emerges and persists. Global sensitivity analysis using Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient combined with Latin Hypercube Sampling indicates that vaccination coverage and vaccine efficacy play a dominant role in reducing R 0 . Although liver transplantation does not affect the magnitude of R 0 , it significantly influences the disease dynamics by reducing the outbreak size and delaying the timing of HBV and HDV outbreaks. These findings indicate that vaccination is essential for reducing transmission, whereas liver transplantation remains important for mitigating severe disease burden; thus, coordinated use of preventive and clinical interventions is needed for effective HBV–HDV control.
abstract_zh: 丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染可严重恶化 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染者的临床结果,因此预防 HBV 感染和治疗严重 HBV-HDV 病例成为重要的公共卫生优先事项。本研究介绍了 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和 D 病毒 (HDV) 传播 的新型数学模型,将 疫苗接种 和肝移植作为疾病控制策略。与允许直接 HDV 感染或一般共感染途径的模型相反,所提出的模型假设 HDV 仅通过已感染 HBV 的个体之间的重复感染而发生。该模型构建为常微分方程组,其中将人群分为易感人群、接种疫苗人群、感染 HBV 的人群、康复人群、慢性人群和 HDV 感染人群。模型分析揭示了无病平衡的存在性和稳定性,当基本再生数(R 0 )小于1时,无病平衡存在且渐近稳定,超过1则不稳定。当R 0 > 1 时,确定了两种类型的地方流行平衡,对应于HDV 感染的不存在和存在。使用 MatCont 进行的连续分析揭示了控制这些平衡之间稳定性转变的两个分支点的存在,突出了 HDV 出现和持续的条件。使用偏秩相关系数结合拉丁超立方抽样的全局敏感性分析表明,疫苗接种 覆盖度和疫苗 功效在降低R 0 方面起主导作用。尽管肝移植不影响R 0 的大小,但它通过减小暴发的大小并延迟HBV和HDV 暴发的时间来显着影响疾病动态。这些发现表明,疫苗接种 对于减少 传播 至关重要,而肝移植对于减轻严重疾病负担仍然很重要;因此,为了有效控制 HBV-HDV,需要协调使用预防和临床干预措施。

title: The Impact of HCC Surveillance on Tumor Features and Receipt of Curative Therapy: A Focus on Chronic Hepatitis B and MASLD.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background As hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) etiologies shift from viral to non‐viral, many at‐risk patients lack surveillance in real‐world practice. This study characterizes the clinical features and receipt of curative therapy in HCC patients with and without surveillance. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at National Taiwan University Hospital (2015–2025). Patients newly diagnosed with HCC who had not undergone regular surveillance ( n = 50) were compared with a consecutive surveillance‐diagnosed cohort ( n = 100). Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with chronic hepatitis B and MASLD. Results Compared with the surveillance group, non‐surveillance patients had higher baseline liver enzymes and alpha‐fetoprotein levels, larger tumors, higher rates of multifocal tumors, and more frequent vascular invasion. Symptomatically diagnosed non‐surveillance patients also presented with more advanced disease. Multivariable analysis identified surveillance as a strong independent predictor of receiving curative therapy (odds ratio [OR]: 17.78; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.56–56.88, p < 0.001). In the chronic hepatitis B subgroup, both surveillance (OR 26.79, 95% CI: 6.80–106.00, p < 0.001) and higher BMI (OR 1.18, 95% CI: 1.05–1.33, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of curative therapy. The rate of HBV carriers (72%), cirrhosis (54%), and MASLD (14%) remained substantial within the non‐surveillance group. Conclusion HCC surveillance was associated with earlier stage at diagnosis and independently predicted receipt of curative therapy; higher BMI was an additional predictor in the HBV subgroup. Most patients diagnosed without surveillance had underlying HBV infection, cirrhosis or MASLD, and presented with more advanced disease and lower rates of curative therapy.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 随着肝细胞癌 (HCC) 病因从病毒转向非病毒,许多高危患者在现实世界中缺乏 监测。本研究描述了患有和不患有 监测 的 HCC 患者的临床特征和接受治疗的情况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 国立台湾大学医院(2015-2025)进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究。将未接受常规 监测 的新诊断 HCC 患者 (n = 50) 与连续接受 监测 诊断的 队列研究 (n = 100) 进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括在国立台湾大学医院(2015-2025)进行的一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,比较使用和未使用 监测 的患者。对 慢性乙型肝炎 和 MASLD 患者进行亚组分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 非 监测 患者的基线肝酶和甲胎蛋白水平较高,肿瘤较大,多灶性肿瘤发生率较高,血管侵犯更频繁。多变量分析确定 监测 是接受治疗的强有力的独立预测因子(比值比 [OR]:17.78;95% 置信区间 [CI]:5.56–56.88,p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HCC 监测 与 诊断 的早期阶段相关,并独立预测接受治疗;较高的 BMI 是 HBV 亚组的另一个预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了 HCC 监测 在提高早期检测和治愈率方面的重要性,特别是对于 慢性乙型肝炎 和 MASLD 患者。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制因果推论的强度。然而,由于 监测 与治疗接受之间存在明确的关联,证据是强有力的。

title: Identification and validation of oxidative stress-related immune signatures in Hepatitis B Virus associated acute liver failure based on WGCNA and machine learning.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute liver failure (ALF) is a serious clinical disease. Immune infiltration and oxidative stress (OS) play an important role in ALF, but the combination of oxidative stress and immune infiltration in ALF has not been explored. METHODS: Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were performed on ALF and control samples in the GSE96851 dataset to obtain DE-OS-MGs. Candidate OS-IM-associated signature genes were mined using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and support vector machine (SVM) machine learning. Finally, OS-IM-related signature genes were obtained by expression analysis and ROC validation. Single gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), TF-miRNA-mRNA network construction and drug prediction were also performed for OS-IM-related signature genes. RESULTS: Differential analysis identified a total of 3580 DEGs in ALF and control samples, and differential analysis of immune cells yielded 15 immune cell species that were significantly different between the two groups. After WGCNA analysis, 1134 key module genes were screened. Then, 3580 DEGs, 855 OS-related genes, and 1134 key module genes were intersected, resulting in a total of 89 DE-OS-MGs. Furthermore, machine learning was performed and the genes were intersected to obtain 5 candidate OS-IM-related signature genes. The expression levels and ROC analysis of the 5 genes were validated in the GSE96851 and GSE120652 datasets, and 4 genes (CLU, APOH, AMBP, and GPX8) were used as biomarkers (OS-IM-related signature genes) for subsequent analysis. Single-gene GSEA enrichment analysis revealed that the 4 biomarkers were associated with metabolic processes. A miRNA-mRNA network with 123 nodes and 194 relationship pairs was obtained. 49 TFs of 3 biomarkers (APOH, AMBP, and GPX8) and 56 relationship pairs of TFs-mRNA regulatory network also constructed. Searching for therapeutic drugs of 4 biomarkers, a drug-mRNA network of CLU and 3 drugs was constructed. CONCLUSION: In this study, we combined immune infiltration landscape and oxidative stress based on bioinformatic analysis to screen for diagnostic markers (CLU, APOH, AMBP, and GPX8) of ALF. It provides a new idea and theoretical basis for the therapeutic diagnosis of ALF.

abstract_zh: 背景:急性肝衰竭(ALF)是一种严重的临床疾病。免疫浸润和氧化应激(OS)在ALF中起重要作用,但ALF中氧化应激与免疫浸润的结合尚未被探索。方法:在GSE96851数据集中对ALF和对照样本进行差异表达分析和加权基因共表达网络分析(WGCNA),以获得DE-OS-MGs。利用最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)和支持向量机(SVM)机器学习方法挖掘候选的OS-IM相关标志物基因。最后,通过表达分析和ROC验证获得OS-IM相关标志物基因。还对OS-IM相关标志物基因进行了单基因集合富集分析(GSEA)、转录因子-微RNA-信使RNA网络构建以及药物预测。结果:差异分析在ALF和对照样本中总共鉴定出3580个差异表达基因(DEGs),免疫细胞差异分析获得了15种在两组间显著不同的免疫细胞类型。经过WGCNA分析后,筛选出1134个关键模块基因。然后,将3580个DEGs、855个氧化应激相关基因和1134个关键模块基因进行交集,总共获得89个DE-OS-MGs。此外,通过机器学习方法对基因进行筛选,最终获得5个候选的OS-IM相关标志物基因。在GSE96851和GSE120652数据集中验证了这5个基因的表达水平和ROC分析,最终确定CLU、APOH、AMBP和GPX8这4个基因作为后续分析的标志物(OS-IM相关标志物基因)。单基因GSEA富集分析显示这4个标志物与代谢过程相关。构建了一个包含123个节点和194个关系对的miRNA-mRNA网络。还构建了3个标志物(APOH、AMBP和GPX8)的49个转录因子(TFs)和TFs-mRNA调控网络的56个关系对。针对4个标志物寻找治疗药物,构建了CLU与3种药物的药物-信使RNA网络。结论:本研究基于生物信息学分析,结合免疫浸润图谱和氧化应激,筛选出ALF的诊断标志物(CLU、APOH、AMBP和GPX8)。这为ALF的治疗诊断提供了新的思路和理论依据。

analysis_zh.methods: 还对 OS-IM 相关特征基因进行了单基因集富集分析 (GSEA)、TF-miRNA-mRNA 网络构建和药物预测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 差异分析在 ALF 和对照样本中总共鉴定出 3580 个 DEG,对免疫细胞的差异分析产生了 15 个免疫细胞种类,两组之间存在显着差异。经过WGCNA分析,筛选出1134个关键模块基因。然后,将3580个DEG、855个OS相关基因和1134个关键模块基因进行交叉,总共得到89个DE-OS-MG。在GSE96851和GSE120652数据集中验证了5个基因的表达水平和ROC分析,并使用4个基因(CLU、APOH、AMBP和GPX8)作为生物标志物(OS-IM相关特征基因)进行后续分析。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解读该研究结果为诊断治疗ALF提供了新的思路和理论依据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果为诊断治疗ALF提供了新的思路和理论依据。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告具体限制或证据强度。

title: Efficacy and Safety of Switching from Entecavir to Tenofovir Alafenamide for Chronic Hepatitis B Patients with Low-Level Viremia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Clinical data on the efficacy and safety of tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with suboptimal response to entecavir (ETV) are limited. This study was designed to investigate the efficacy and safety of switching to TAF in CHB patients with low-level viremia (LLV). METHODS: CHB patients with LLV who received ETV treatment for more than 52 weeks were divided into TAF group (n = 104) and ETV group (n = 395). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences in age between the two groups. The outcomes included complete virological response (CVR) at weeks 12 and 24, normalization rates of aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and renal function and blood lipid levels. RESULTS: Compared with the ETV group, the TAF group had significantly higher rates of CVR at week 12 and week 24 in both the raw cohort and the PSM cohort (all P 0.05). CONCLUSION: Switching to TAF may be beneficial for patients with LLV after prolonged ETV therapy, as it is associated with a significantly higher rate of CVR. No lipid metabolism-related disorders were observed following the switch to TAF.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of switching from entecavir (ETV) to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with low-level viremia (LLV). The research was motivated by the limited clinical data on TAF in this patient group. A total of 499 patients were divided into TAF group (n = 104) and ETV group (n = 395). Propensity score matching was used to adjust for age differences. The outcomes included complete virological response (CVR) at weeks 12 and 24, normalization of ALT and AST levels, and assessments of renal function and blood lipid levels. The authors concluded that switching to TAF may be beneficial for patients with LLV after prolonged ETV therapy. The study's findings could inform treatment strategies for CHB patients with LLV, but the evidence is limited to a single cohort and lacks long-term follow-up data.

abstract_zh: OBJECTIVE: 替诺福韦艾拉酚胺富马酸盐(TAF)在对恩替卡韦(ETV)反应不佳的慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中的疗效和安全性临床数据有限。本研究旨在探讨在慢性乙型肝炎患者中,从恩替卡韦转换为TAF对低水平病毒血症(LLV)患者的疗效和安全性。METHODS: 接受恩替卡韦治疗超过52周且具有低水平病毒血症的CHB患者被分为TAF组(n = 104)和ETV组(n = 395)。采用倾向评分匹配(PSM)调整两组间基线年龄的差异。研究结果包括第12周和第24周的完全病毒学反应(CVR)率、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)水平正常化率,以及肾功能和血脂水平。RESULTS: 与ETV组相比,TAF组在原始数据和倾向评分匹配数据中,第12周和第24周的CVR率均显著更高(所有P < 0.05)。CONCLUSION: 对于接受长期恩替卡韦治疗后出现低水平病毒血症的患者,转换为TAF可能具有益处,因为它与更高的CVR率相关。转换为TAF后未观察到与血脂代谢相关的疾病。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在调查低水平病毒血症 (LLV) 慢性乙型肝炎患者改用 TAF 的有效性和安全性。接受ETV 治疗超过52周的伴有LLV的CHB患者分为TAF组(n = 104)和ETV组(n = 395)。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用倾向评分匹配(PSM)调整两组间基线年龄的差异。研究结果包括第12周和第24周的完全病毒学反应(CVR)率、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)水平正常化率,以及肾功能和血脂水平。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与 ETV 组相比,TAF 组在第 12 周和第 24 周时原始 队列研究 和 PSM 队列研究 的 CVR 率均显着升高(均 P < 0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 长期 ETV 治疗后改用 TAF 可能对 LLV 患者有益,因为它与显着较高的 CVR 率相关。

title: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development in Patients With Hepatitis B Virus-Related Cirrhosis Receiving Antiviral Therapy.
abstract: Few prediction models have been specifically designed to evaluate the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients with chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based prediction model to assess the risk of developing HCC in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis undergoing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy. We included 1592 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis who had received entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, or tenofovir alafenamide for at least 1 year. Patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio into derivation or validation groups, and the prediction model was developed using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm. The cumulative incidence of HCC for all patients at 5, 8, and 10 years was 15.2%, 22.7%, and 25.7%, respectively. Our ML-HCC model incorporated six parameters: serum albumin and platelet count at treatment initiation, and age, platelet count, serum aspartate transaminase, and serum AFP after 1 year of NA therapy. In the validation group, the AUROCs of the ML-HCC model ranged from 0.79 to 0.80 over 3 to 10 years, outperforming extant models including APA-B, PLAN-B, PAGE-B, mPAGE-B, REACH-B, and CU-HCC (AUROCs: 0.61-0.73, p < 0.05). Risk stratification showed the 10-year incidences of HCC for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups were 9%, 26%, and 67%, respectively. The proposed machine learning model for predicting development of HCC exhibited good predictive performance in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis undergoing NA therapy.
journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

elements_zh.methods: 所提出的预测 HCC 发展的机器学习模型在接受 NA 治疗的 HBV 相关肝硬化患者中表现出良好的预测性能。

analysis_zh.main_results: 所有患者在5、8和10年时HCC的累积发生率分别为15.2%、22.7%和25.7%。在验证组中,ML-HCC模型在3至10年期间的AUROCs范围为0.79至0.80,优于现有模型包括APA-B、PLAN-B、PAGE-B、mPAGE-B、REACH-B和CU-HCC(AUROCs:0.61-0.73,p < 0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的ML-HCC模型整合了六个参数:在治疗开始时的血清白蛋白和血小板计数,以及接受NA治疗1年后的年龄、血小板计数、血清天门冬氨酸转氨酶和血清甲胎蛋白。该模型的预测性能优于现有模型,表明其为HBV相关肝硬化患者风险评估提供了一种新的方法。

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, Self-Reported Practices, and Self-Reported Hepatitis B Vaccination Completion Among Dental Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dental students are exposed to blood-borne pathogens and sharps injuries, making adherence to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures essential for their safety. This study compared IPC knowledge, attitudes, self-reported practices, and self-reported hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination completion between fourth- and fifth-year dental students. METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire study included separate fourth- and fifth-year dental-student cohorts at the College of Dentistry, Al-Mustansiriyah University, Baghdad, Iraq. The investigator-developed, context-adapted questionnaire comprised 12 knowledge, 10 attitude, and 12 self-reported practice items. We used Mann-Whitney U and chi-squared tests for academic-year comparisons, with Holm adjustment applied to the prespecified families of KAP comparisons. RESULTS: The study included 188 participants: 95 fourth-year students (79.4% response rate) and 93 fifth-year students (77.5% response rate). Fifth-year students had higher knowledge scores than fourth-year students (median [interquartile range], 11 [10-12] vs. 9 [8-9]; Holm-adjusted p < 0.003; r = 0.70), greater knowledge adequacy (97.8% vs. 55.8%; Holm-adjusted p < 0.003), and a higher prevalence of self-reported completion of the three-dose HBV vaccination schedule (60.2% vs. 31.6%; p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.29). Attitude and self-reported practice scores were high in both cohorts, with comparatively smaller between-cohort differences. CONCLUSION: The two cohorts differed principally in IPC knowledge and self-reported HBV vaccination completion. Because the study was cross-sectional, the findings do not demonstrate within-student improvement or the causal effect of academic progression.

METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire study included separate fourth- and fifth-year dental-student cohorts at the College of Dentistry, Al-Mustansiriyah University, Baghdad, Iraq. The investigator-developed, context-adapted questionnaire comprised 12 knowledge, 10 attitude, and 12 self-reported practice items. We used Mann-Whitney U and chi-squared tests for academic-year comparisons, with Holm adjustment applied to the prespecified families of KAP comparisons. RESULTS: The study included 188 participants: 95 fourth-year students (79.4% response rate) and 93 fifth-year students (77.5% response rate). Fifth-year students had higher knowledge scores than fourth-year students (median [interquartile range], 11 [10-12] vs. 9 [8-9]; Holm-adjusted p < 0.003; r = 0.70), greater knowledge adequacy (97.8% vs. 55.8%; Holm-adjusted p < 0.003), and a higher prevalence of self-reported completion of the three-dose HBV vaccination schedule (60.2% vs. 31.6%; p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.29). Attitude and self-reported practice scores were high in both cohorts, with comparatively smaller between-cohort differences. CONCLUSION: The two cohorts differed principally in IPC knowledge and self-reported HBV vaccination completion. Because the study was cross-sectional, the findings do not demonstrate within-student improvement or the causal effect of academic progression.

abstract_zh: 背景:牙科学生接触血液传播病原体和锐器伤害,因此遵守感染预防与控制(IPC)措施对其安全至关重要。本研究比较了第四年和第五年牙科学生的IPC知识、态度、自我报告实践以及自我报告的三剂HBV疫苗接种完成情况。方法:本项横断面问卷调查包括伊拉克巴格达阿必须萨里耶大学牙学院的第四年和第五年牙科学生的独立样本。由研究者开发并根据情境调整的问卷包含12个知识问题、10个态度问题和12个自我报告实践问题。我们使用Mann-Whitney U检验和卡方检验进行学年间的比较,并对预设的KAP比较家族应用Holm校正。结果:研究共纳入188名参与者,其中第四年学生95名(响应率79.4%),第五年学生93名(响应率77.5%)。第五年学生的知识得分高于第四年学生(中位数[四分位数范围],11[10-12] vs. 9[8-9];Holm校正后p < 0.003;r = 0.70),知识充分性更高(97.8% vs. 55.8%;Holm校正后p < 0.003),并且自我报告的三剂HBV疫苗接种完成率更高(60.2% vs. 31.6%;p < 0.001;Cramer's V = 0.29)。在两个学年中,态度和自我报告实践得分均较高,但学年间的差异相对较小。结论:两个学年在IPC知识和自我报告的HBV疫苗接种完成情况上存在主要差异。由于本研究是横断面研究,因此研究结果无法显示学生内部的改善或学术进展的因果效应。

title: Longitudinal Adherence Trajectories of First-Line Nucleotide Analogues among US Older Adults with Chronic Hepatitis B.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of first-line nucleot(s)side analogs (NAs) for managing chronic hepatitis B (CHB) depends heavily on treatment adherence; however, evidence on longitudinal adherence patterns is limited, especially in older adults. OBJECTIVE: This study examined longitudinal adherence trajectories of NAs among older adults with CHB. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study involved continuously enrolled Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with CHB from 2014-2019. Monthly adherence was evaluated using proportion of days covered for incident NAs users, specifically entecavir (ETV), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Longitudinal adherence patterns were analyzed using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) over a 12-month follow-up. The variation in adherence trajectories across first-line NAs was examined using a multinomial logistic regression model, adjusted for baseline covariates. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 3,317 older adults with CHB, with a mean age of 72.6 years, and 57.85% were men. The GBTM identified three long-term adherence patterns: consistently adherent (56.89%), gradual decline (24.78%), and rapid decline (18.33%). The consistently adherent patients varied across the individual NAs (ETV = 52.21%, TDF = 57.39%, and TAF = 71.06%). Multinomial logistic model found that patients on TAF had 0.41 times lower odds of being rapid decliners (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34-0.49) and 0.45 times lower odds of being gradual decliners (95%CI: 0.39-0.53), compared to ETV. CONCLUSIONS: Over half of older adults with CHB consistently adhered to NAs, with significant variation in adherence patterns across the individual NAs. Overall, TAF was less likely to be associated with declining adherence patterns than other NAs. Understanding these long-term adherence patterns can help in developing targeted interventions to improve CHB care in older adults.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated longitudinal adherence trajectories of first-line nucleotide analogs (NAs) among older adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the US. The research aimed to address the limited evidence on adherence patterns in this population, as adherence significantly impacts the effectiveness of NA treatment. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on continuously enrolled Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with CHB from 2014 to 2019. Monthly adherence was assessed using the proportion of days covered for incident users of entecavir (ETV), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) identified three adherence patterns: consistently adherent (56.89%), gradual decline (24.78%), and rapid decline (18.33%). The multinomial logistic regression model revealed that TAF was associated with lower odds of declining adherence compared to ETV. These findings highlight the importance of understanding adherence patterns to improve CHB management in older adults. The study provides valuable insights into treatment adherence but does not report limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 一线核苷酸类似物 (NA) 治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 的有效性在很大程度上取决于 治疗 的依从性;然而,关于纵向依从模式的证据有限,特别是在老年人中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性 队列研究 研究涉及 2014 年至 2019 年连续登记的年龄≥ 65 岁的慢性乙型肝炎医疗保险受益人。
elements_zh.methods: 使用事件 NA 用户的覆盖天数比例评估每月依从性,特别是恩替卡韦 (ETV)、富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 和替诺福韦艾拉酚胺 (TAF)。在 12 个月的随访中,使用基于组的轨迹模型 (GBTM) 分析纵向依从模式。使用多项逻辑回归模型检查一线 NA 的依从轨迹的变化,并根据基线协变量进行调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 队列研究 的研究由 3,317 名患有慢性乙型肝炎的老年人组成,平均年龄为 72.6 岁,其中 57.85% 为男性。GBTM 确定了三种长期坚持模式:持续坚持(56.89%)、逐渐下降(24.78%)和快速下降(18.33%)。坚持依从的患者在各个 NA 中存在差异(ETV = 52.21%、TDF = 57.39% 和 TAF = 71.06%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多项 Logistic 模型发现,与 ETV 相比,接受 TAF 治疗的患者快速衰退的几率降低了 0.41 倍(95% 置信区间 [CI]:0.34-0.49),逐渐衰退的几率降低了 0.45 倍(95%CI:0.39-0.53)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 了解这些长期依从模式有助于制定有针对性的干预措施,以改善老年人的慢性乙型肝炎护理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

The variation in adherence trajectories across first-line NAs was examined using a multinomial logistic regression model, adjusted for baseline covariates. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 3,317 older adults with CHB, with a mean age of 72.6 years, and 57.85% were men. The GBTM identified three long-term adherence patterns: consistently adherent (56.89%), gradual decline (24.78%), and rapid decline (18.33%). The consistently adherent patients varied across the individual NAs (ETV = 52.21%, TDF = 57.39%, and TAF = 71.06%). Multinomial logistic model found that patients on TAF had 0.41 times lower odds of being rapid decliners (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34-0.49) and 0.45 times lower odds of being gradual decliners (95%CI: 0.39-0.53), compared to ETV. CONCLUSIONS: Over half of older adults with CHB consistently adhered to NAs, with significant variation in adherence patterns across the individual NAs. Overall, TAF was less likely to be associated with declining adherence patterns than other NAs. Understanding these long-term adherence patterns can help in developing targeted interventions to improve CHB care in older adults.

title: Hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in haploidentical versus matched donor transplantation: Impact of universal prophylaxis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus reactivation is a serious complication of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, particularly in endemic regions. Patients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive serology represent an intermediate-risk group due to occult hepatitis B virus infection. This study evaluated hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in haploidentical versus matched donor hematopoietic cell transplantation and assessed the effectiveness of Taiwan's universal prophylaxis policy. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 165 adult hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive status was conducted at China Medical University Hospital, Taiwan from 2010-2025. The incidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation was compared between the pre-prophylaxis (2010-February 2021) and post-policy implementation (March 2021-2025) periods. Univariable associations, clinical outcomes, and temporal patterns were analyzed. RESULTS: Pre-prophylaxis, haploidentical recipients had higher reactivation rates (11.2%vs. 2.9%), but this did not reach statistical significance due to the small number of events (Odds ratio: 4.31; 95% CI: 0.67-37.55; p = 0.279). In the univariable analyses, hepatitis B virus reactivation was associated with chronic graft-versus-host disease (p = 0.001) and donor anti-HBs negativity (p = 0.001), with a median time to reactivation of 8.2 months. CONCLUSION: In this cohort, haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide was associated with a higher observed rate of hepatitis B virus reactivation than matched donor transplantation in HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive recipients, although this difference was not statistically significant.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 单倍体相合移植与匹配供体移植中的再激活风险:普遍预防的影响。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus reactivation is a serious complication of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, particularly in endemic regions. Patients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive serology represent an intermediate-risk group due to occult hepatitis B virus infection. This study evaluated hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in haploidentical versus matched donor hematopoietic cell transplantation and assessed the effectiveness of Taiwan's universal prophylaxis policy. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 165 adult hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive status was conducted at China Medical University Hospital, Taiwan from 2010-2025. The incidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation was compared between the pre-prophylaxis (2010-February 2021) and post-policy implementation (March 2021-2025) periods. Univariable associations, clinical outcomes, and temporal patterns were analyzed. RESULTS: Pre-prophylaxis, haploidentical recipients had higher reactivation rates (11.2%vs. 2.9%), but this did not reach statistical significance due to the small number of events (Odds ratio: 4.31; 95% CI: 0.67-37.55; p = 0.279). In the univariable analyses, hepatitis B virus reactivation was associated with chronic graft-versus-host disease (p = 0.001) and donor anti-HBs negativity (p = 0.001), with a median time to reactivation of 8.2 months. CONCLUSION: In this cohort, haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide was associated with a higher observed rate of hepatitis B virus reactivation than matched donor transplantation in HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive recipients, although this difference was not statistically significant.
abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒 再激活是同种异体造血细胞移植的严重并发症,特别是在流行地区。由于隐匿性 乙型肝炎病毒 感染,HBsAg 阴性/抗 HBc 阳性 血清学 患者属于中危人群。本研究评估了半相合与匹配供体造血细胞移植中的 乙型肝炎病毒 再激活风险,并评估了台湾普遍预防政策的有效性。方法:2010-2025 年在台湾中国医科大学医院对 165 名 HBsAg 阴性/抗 HBc 阳性的成人造血细胞移植受者进行了回顾性 队列研究 研究。比较预防前(2010年至2021年2月)和政策实施后(2021年3月至2025年3月)期间乙型肝炎病毒重新激活的发病率。分析了单变量关联、临床结果和时间模式。结果:预防前,半相合受者的再激活率较高(11.2% vs. 2.9%),但由于事件数量较少,因此并未达到统计学显着性(优势比:4.31;95% CI:0.67-37.55;p = 0.279)。在单变量分析中,乙型肝炎病毒 再激活与慢性移植物抗 宿主 疾病 (p = 0.001) 和供体抗 HBs 阴性 (p = 0.001) 相关,中位再激活时间为 8.2 个月。结论:在该 队列研究 中,在 HBsAg 阴性/抗 HBc 阳性受者中,使用移植后环磷酰胺的半相合造血细胞移植与观察到的 乙型肝炎病毒 再激活率高于匹配供体移植相关,尽管这种差异不具有统计学意义。

title: Prevention practices toward hepatitis B virus and associated factors among male barbers in the selected districts in Mogadishu, Somalia: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background: Male barbers may contribute to hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission through occupational exposure to blood and contaminated instruments. However, evidence on HBV prevention practices among barbers in Somalia is limited. This study assessed the level of HBV prevention practices and factors associated with these practices among male barbers in selected districts of Mogadishu, Somalia. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among male barbers working in registered and non-registered barbershops in Daynile, Hodan, Howl-Wadag, and Yaqshid districts of Mogadishu from 1 to 29 July 2026. A total of 768 eligible male barbers constituted the sampling frame, from which 384 participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, occupational factors, HBV-related knowledge and attitudes, and prevention practices. Prevention practices were classified as safe when participants correctly answered more than 50% of 12 practice questions. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with safe prevention practices. Results: Among the 384 participating barbers, 249 (64.84%) demonstrated unsafe HBV prevention practices, while 135 (35.16%) demonstrated safe practices. After adjustment, educational level, working hours, work experience, monthly income, and knowledge level were significantly associated with prevention practices. Barbers with no formal education had lower odds of safe practices than those with formal education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.12–0.55). Those working ≥ 8 hours per day had lower odds of safe practices than those working Conclusion: Unsafe HBV prevention practices were common among male barbers in selected districts of Mogadishu. The findings indicate important gaps in routine infection prevention and suggest that educational, occupational, and economic conditions influence the implementation of safer practices. Targeted practical infection-control training, periodic refresher education, improved access to affordable prevention materials, and strengthened HBV screening and vaccination services should be considered to reduce occupational and community risks of HBV transmission among barbers in Mogadishu.

source_body_en: Abstract Background: Male barbers may contribute to hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission through occupational exposure to blood and contaminated instruments. However, evidence on HBV prevention practices among barbers in Somalia is limited. This study assessed the level of HBV prevention practices and factors associated with these practices among male barbers in selected districts of Mogadishu, Somalia. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among male barbers working in registered and non-registered barbershops in Daynile, Hodan, Howl-Wadag, and Yaqshid districts of Mogadishu from 1 to 29 July 2026. A total of 768 eligible male barbers constituted the sampling frame, from which 384 participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, occupational factors, HBV-related knowledge and attitudes, and prevention practices. Prevention practices were classified as safe when participants correctly answered more than 50% of 12 practice questions. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with safe prevention practices. Results: Among the 384 participating barbers, 249 (64.84%) demonstrated unsafe HBV prevention practices, while 135 (35.16%) demonstrated safe practices. After adjustment, educational level, working hours, work experience, monthly income, and knowledge level were significantly associated with prevention practices. Barbers with no formal education had lower odds of safe practices than those with formal education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.12–0.55). Those working ≥ 8 hours per day had lower odds of safe practices than those working Conclusion: Unsafe HBV prevention practices were common among male barbers in selected districts of Mogadishu. The findings indicate important gaps in routine infection prevention and suggest that educational, occupational, and economic conditions influence the implementation of safer practices. Targeted practical infection-control training, periodic refresher education, improved access to affordable prevention materials, and strengthened HBV screening and vaccination services should be considered to reduce occupational and community risks of HBV transmission among barbers in Mogadishu.

title: Hepatitis B and C Knowledge, Testing Uptake, and Vaccination Coverage Among Men Aged 15-49 in Nepal: A Nationally Representative Analysis of the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey
abstract: Abstract Background Nepal has integrated the commitment for hepatitis B and C as a public health threat into its National Strategy for Viral Hepatitis B and C(2023–2030). While the prevalence of chronic hepatitis in the general population is lower in Nepal, knowledge, testing and vaccination need to be known for potential elimination of viral hepatitis in this age group. Males are relatively under-represented in reproductive and child health surveys, but males’ knowledge and health-seeking behavior influence the household approach for prevention and hepatitis care cascade. The gendered study aims to assess the knowledge of hepatitis B and C, its sociodemographic determinants, and testing using the NDHS (2022) among males aged 15–49 years. Methods We used the data from the men’s recode dataset (NPMR82FL) of the 2022 NDHS, a cross-sectional nationally representative survey. The knowledge about Hepatitis was recorded as a composite variable from three items available on a binary response format in men’s module (hepatitis C is transmitted through blood, hepatitis C can be prevented, hepatitis B can be cured). The score was categorized into adequate and inadequate knowledge based on the median cut-off. The survey-weighted estimation (svydesign function in R) was used for adjusting for primary sampling unit (mv021), strata (mv022) and sampling weights (mv005/1,000,000). Weighted prevalence of adequate knowledge was calculated by province, wealth quintile, age group, place of residence and ecological zone. Factors associated with knowledge were studied through survey-weighted linear regression (continuous score) and logistic regression (adequate knowledge). Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals were reported. Receiver operating curve and area under the curve (ROC-AUC) was used to check the discrimination ability of the model. Concentration index was used to find out the equity related with knowledge of hepatitis on wealth quintile. A five-fold cross-validation procedure was used for internal validation. Results After applying survey weights, the prevalence of adequate knowledge varied significantly by province: Gandaki, 81.5% (95% CI: 76.5–86.5) and Sudurpashchim, 76.3% (72.1–80.5) were among the higher provinces and Madhesh was the lowest, at 58.0% (53.7–62.2). There was a clear wealth gradient for adequate knowledge, with 65.3% (61.8–68.9) in the poorest quintile to 82.0% (79.2–84.9) for the richest quintile. Logistic regression modeling for determinants of adequate knowledge showed that higher levels of education were the strongest predictor (compared to no education: secondary: aOR 3.48, 95% CI 2.56–4.72; higher education: aOR 7.09, 4.10-12.25). Other positive predictors were older age (35–49: aOR 1.85, 1.38–2.48); internet use (aOR 1.65, 1.35–2.02); and residence in the Hill ecological zone (aOR 1.45, 1.04–2.02). Significantly lower odds of adequate knowledge were found among men living in the Madhesh (aOR 0.53, 0.39–0.71) and Karnali (aOR 0.67, 0.47–0.97) provinces, compared to those living in the Koshi province. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.703) and moderate explanatory power (McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.087) while the concentration index was − 0.030 indicating a slight pro-poor distribution of knowledge. Cross-validation indicated mean accuracy of 0.727 and mean AUC of 0.693. The proportion of respondents tested for hepatitis was available for only 23 respondents (99.5% missing), precluding any analysis regarding the testing uptake. Vaccination coverage data was not collected from the module for men. Conclusions Hepatitis knowledge disparities among Nepali men vary with education, geography and internet access. There are significant provincial differences in access to knowledge. While knowledge levels in absolute terms appear to be relatively high, the fact that nearly a third of men in the country lack adequate knowledge, particularly restrictive in targeted provinces such as Madhesh and Karnali, as well as household wealth indicates that there were fissures in health literacy that need to be addressed. The lack of hepatitis testing or vaccination status data among male respondents in the DHS module is a key surveillance gap that hinders the monitoring of Nepal’s hepatitis elimination progress and pathway to the 2030 elimination goals. It is recommended that these hepatitis indicators be included in future rounds of male questionnaires in the DHS and in national health information systems to provide for appropriate gender-disaggregated cascade monitoring.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess knowledge of hepatitis B and C, its sociodemographic determinants, and testing uptake among men aged 15–49 in Nepal to support elimination efforts. The background highlights Nepal's commitment to addressing viral hepatitis as a public health threat and the need to understand knowledge, testing and vaccination for potential elimination in this age group.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional nationally representative survey was conducted using the men’s recode dataset from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS). The study focused on males aged 15–49 years across Nepal, with data analyzed by province, wealth quintile, age group, place of residence, and ecological zone.
analysis.methods: The study used survey-weighted linear and logistic regression models to analyze factors associated with adequate hepatitis knowledge. The survey-weighted estimation was adjusted for primary sampling unit, strata, and sampling weights using the svydesign function in R. The model's discrimination ability was assessed using the receiver operating curve and area under the curve (ROC-AUC), while the concentration index evaluated equity in knowledge distribution by wealth quintile.
analysis.main_results: After applying survey weights, the prevalence of adequate hepatitis knowledge varied significantly by province, with Gandaki at 81.5% (95% CI: 76.5–86.5) and Sudurpashchim at 76.3% (72.1–80.5) being among the higher provinces, while Madhesh had the lowest at 58.0% (53.7–62.2). There was a clear wealth gradient, with 65.3% (61.8–68.9) in the poorest quintile and 82.0% (79.2–84.9) in the richest quintile having adequate knowledge. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.703) and moderate explanatory power (McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.087), with a concentration index of −0.030 indicating a slight pro-poor distribution of knowledge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that knowledge disparities among Nepali men are influenced by education, geography, and internet access. The study's novelty lies in its focus on male-specific knowledge and its contribution to understanding the factors affecting health literacy in this demographic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted public health interventions to improve hepatitis knowledge in provinces with lower coverage, such as Madhesh and Karnali, and highlight the need for gender-disaggregated surveillance to monitor progress toward hepatitis elimination goals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has limitations due to the lack of hepatitis testing or vaccination status data among male respondents, which precludes analysis of testing uptake and vaccination coverage. Despite this, the evidence is moderate in strength, supported by survey-weighted regression models and cross-validation procedures.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed hepatitis B and C knowledge among Nepali men aged 15–49 using data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. It found significant provincial and wealth-related disparities in knowledge, with higher levels in Gandaki and Sudurpashchim and lower in Madhesh. Education, age, internet use, and ecological zone were identified as key predictors of adequate knowledge. The study highlights the need for improved gender-disaggregated surveillance and targeted interventions to address health literacy gaps. However, the lack of testing and vaccination data limits the analysis of uptake and coverage, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2022 年尼泊尔人口和健康调查 (NDHS) 的男性重新编码数据集进行了一项具有全国代表性的横断面调查。该研究重点关注尼泊尔 15 至 49 岁的男性,按省份、财富五分位数、年龄组、居住地和生态区对数据进行分析。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏男性受访者的肝炎检测或 疫苗接种 状态数据,该研究存在局限性,这妨碍了对检测采用率和 疫苗接种 覆盖率的分析。尽管如此,证据强度适中,并得到调查加权回归模型和交叉验证程序的支持。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2022 年尼泊尔人口和健康调查 (NDHS) 的男性重新编码数据集进行了一项具有全国代表性的横断面调查。该研究重点关注尼泊尔 15 至 49 岁的男性,按省份、财富五分位数、年龄组、居住地和生态区对数据进行分析。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,尼泊尔男性之间的知识差距受到教育、地理和互联网接入的影响。该研究的新颖之处在于其重点关注男性特定知识及其对了解影响该人群健康素养的因素的贡献。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为在知识覆盖率较低的省份(如马德什和卡纳利省)开展有针对性的公共卫生干预措施提供了信息,并强调了需要进行性别分层的监测监测以实现肝炎消除目标。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏男性受访者的肝炎检测或 疫苗接种 状态数据,该研究存在局限性,这妨碍了对检测采用率和 疫苗接种 覆盖率的分析。尽管如此,证据强度适中,并得到调查加权回归模型和交叉验证程序的支持。

title: Association of alanine aminotransferase flares with hepatitis B surface antigen loss and clinical outcomes in treated and untreated patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection: A US retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous research has demonstrated the clinical significance of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) flares; however, studies have mostly been in Asian countries or populations, and it remains unclear whether ALT flares during treatment are associated with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss and long-term adverse clinical outcomes. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between ALT flares and virologic outcomes (HBsAg and hepatitis B e antigen [HBeAg] loss) as well as adverse clinical outcomes among patients with chronic hepatitis B in the United States, according to treatment status. DESIGN: Retrospective study using the Optum de-identified electronic health record dataset (2012-2019). METHODS: Marginal structural models estimated the associations between ALT flares and outcomes, accounting for time-varying confounding; adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were reported. A Cox proportional hazards regression model was used to assess risk factors for flares. RESULTS: 14,328 patients were included in the untreated cohort; of these, 2298 (16.0%) initiated and 1541 (10.7%) subsequently discontinued treatment. At least one ALT flare was experienced by 364 patients (2.5%) in the untreated cohort, 84 (3.7%) in the treatment initiation cohort, and 22 (1.4%) in the discontinuation cohort. Risk factors for ALT flares in the untreated group included male sex, history of flares, metabolic syndrome, liver fibrosis, compensated cirrhosis (CC), and hepatic decompensation. Risk factors after treatment initiation included younger age, White race, history of flares, and evidence of liver damage (liver fibrosis, CC, or hepatic decompensation). Flares in the untreated group were associated with spontaneous HBsAg loss and with an increased risk of hepatic decompensation, hospitalization, and death. Flares after treatment initiation were associated with HBsAg and HBeAg loss but not with adverse clinical outcomes investigated. CONCLUSION: ALT flares in untreated patients were associated with virologic and adverse clinical outcomes; no association with adverse clinical outcomes was observed in patients who initiated treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between alanine aminotransferase (ALT) flares and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in the United States. It evaluates whether ALT flares are linked to HBsAg loss and adverse outcomes in both treated and untreated populations. The study uses a retrospective cohort design based on the Optum electronic health record dataset from 2012 to 2019. Results show that ALT flares in untreated patients are associated with spontaneous HBsAg loss and increased risk of hepatic decompensation, hospitalization, and death. In contrast, flares after treatment initiation are linked to HBsAg and HBeAg loss but not to adverse clinical outcomes. The authors conclude that ALT flares have different implications depending on treatment status, highlighting the need for further research to understand their role in HBV management. The study's limitations include its observational design and potential biases inherent in electronic health record data, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 先前的研究已经证明了丙氨酸转氨酶 (ALT) 升高的临床意义;然而,研究大多是在亚洲国家或人群中进行,目前尚不清楚 治疗 期间 ALT 升高是否与乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 丢失和长期不良临床结果相关。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 Optum 去识别化电子健康记录数据集(2012-2019)进行回顾性研究。在未治疗的队列研究中,有364名患者(2.5%)经历了至少一次ALT发作,在治疗起始队列研究中,有84名患者(3.7%),在终止队列研究中,有22名患者(1.4%)经历过至少一次ALT耀斑。
elements_zh.methods: 边际结构模型估计了 ALT 耀斑和结果之间的关联,并考虑了随时间变化的混杂因素;报告了调整后的比值比和 95% 置信区间。Cox 比例风险回归模型用于评估耀斑的风险因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 未经治疗的 队列研究 纳入了 14,328 名患者;其中,2298 名 (16.0%) 发起了 治疗,1541 名 (10.7%) 随后终止了 治疗。未经治疗组的耀斑与 HBsAg 自发消失有关,并且肝功能失代偿、住院和死亡的风险增加。治疗 启动后的耀斑与 HBsAg 和 HBeAg 消失相关,但与所调查的不良临床结果无关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 未经治疗的患者中 ALT 升高与病毒学和不良临床结果相关;在开始 治疗 的患者中未观察到与不良临床结果相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为 监测 和 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的风险评估策略提供信息,特别是在了解 ALT 耀斑在预测 HBsAg 消失和不良临床结果中的作用方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,基于电子健康记录,这可能会引入偏见并限制建立因果关系的能力。由于该研究的观察性质,证据的强度中等。

title: Hepatitis B Virus: Epidemiology, Prophylaxis, Therapy, Clinical Outcomes, and Novel Therapeutic Directions
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a worldwide health concern that infects nearly 254 million people globally and causes more than 1 million deaths annually. The highest prevalence is seen in sub-Saharan Africa and the Western Pacific region. Cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are reported as leading complications of chronic HBV. The route of transmission of this infection is mainly by exposure to infected blood and bodily fluids. Transmission from mother-to-child remains the predominant route in highly endemic areas. Vaccination has significantly reduced HBV seroprevalence and complications. However, incomplete vaccination of newborns continues to be a major obstacle to elimination of the disease. Current prevention strategies include universal vaccination, perinatal prophylaxis with hepatitis B immune globulin, and maternal antiviral therapy in pregnant women with high viral load. The management of chronic hepatitis B virus infection predominantly depends on nucleoside analogs, including entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, and tenofovir alafenamide, as well as pegylated interferon alfa. These therapies effectively suppress viral replication and reduce the risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and liver-related mortality, but they rarely achieve functional cure characterized by hepatitis B surface antigen loss. The persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) remains a major hindrance in HBV eradication. Therefore, novel therapeutic strategies targeting different stages of the viral life cycle, including capsid assembly modulators, small interfering RNAs, nucleic acid polymers, and cccDNA-directed approaches, are under active investigation. This review summarizes the epidemiology, prevention, current therapies, clinical outcomes, and emerging therapeutic advances in HBV infection, highlighting ongoing efforts toward achieving a functional cure and global HBV elimination.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒:流行病学、预防、治疗、临床结果和新颖的治疗方向
source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a worldwide health concern that infects nearly 254 million people globally and causes more than 1 million deaths annually. The highest prevalence is seen in sub-Saharan Africa and the Western Pacific region. Cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are reported as leading complications of chronic HBV. The route of transmission of this infection is mainly by exposure to infected blood and bodily fluids. Transmission from mother-to-child remains the predominant route in highly endemic areas. Vaccination has significantly reduced HBV seroprevalence and complications. However, incomplete vaccination of newborns continues to be a major obstacle to elimination of the disease. Current prevention strategies include universal vaccination, perinatal prophylaxis with hepatitis B immune globulin, and maternal antiviral therapy in pregnant women with high viral load. The management of chronic hepatitis B virus infection predominantly depends on nucleoside analogs, including entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, and tenofovir alafenamide, as well as pegylated interferon alfa. These therapies effectively suppress viral replication and reduce the risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and liver-related mortality, but they rarely achieve functional cure characterized by hepatitis B surface antigen loss. The persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) remains a major hindrance in HBV eradication. Therefore, novel therapeutic strategies targeting different stages of the viral life cycle, including capsid assembly modulators, small interfering RNAs, nucleic acid polymers, and cccDNA-directed approaches, are under active investigation. This review summarizes the epidemiology, prevention, current therapies, clinical outcomes, and emerging therapeutic advances in HBV infection, highlighting ongoing efforts toward achieving a functional cure and global HBV elimination.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本综述总结了 流行病学、预防、当前治疗、临床结果和 HBV 感染的新兴治疗进展,强调了为实现 功能性治愈 和全球 HBV 消除而正在进行的努力。
analysis_zh.methods: 慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染的治疗主要依赖于核苷类似物,包括恩替卡韦、富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯和替诺福韦艾拉酚胺,以及聚乙二醇化干扰素α。
analysis_zh.main_results: 据报道,肝硬化、肝功能衰竭和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 是慢性乙型肝炎的主要并发症。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 目前的预防策略包括通用 疫苗接种、乙型肝炎免疫球蛋白围产期预防以及高病毒载量孕妇的孕产妇 抗病毒药物 治疗。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 疫苗接种 显着减少了 HBV 血清流行率 和并发症。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 然而,新生儿疫苗接种的不完全仍然是消除该疾病的主要障碍。

title: Barriers to Viral Hepatitis Elimination and New Strategies to Overcome Them in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
abstract: Chronic infections with hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis D virus (HDV) are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. The greatest burden is borne by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite the availability of highly effective preventive tools, simplified diagnostics, and affordable antiviral therapies, progress toward the World Health Organization's (WHO) goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030 is insufficient in most LMICs. Gaps persist throughout the entire care continuum, from vaccination and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission to screening, confirmatory testing, linkage to care, treatment initiation, and long-term follow-up. Structural weaknesses in health systems, limited laboratory infrastructure, centralised models of care, financial constraints, stigma, and fragmented disease-specific programmes continue to hinder large-scale implementation. This article examines the main barriers encountered across the viral hepatitis care cascade, from prevention and testing to treatment and long-term follow-up. It discusses practical approaches to overcoming them, including simplified diagnostic and treatment pathways, point-of-care and near-point-of-care technologies, self-testing, integrated testing platforms, decentralised care, and task sharing. Attention is given to the prevention of mother-to-child transmission, the needs of populations underserved by conventional healthcare systems, and comorbidities that influence liver disease progression. In conclusion, technological advances alone will not be sufficient. Progress will also depend on stronger health systems, decentralised models of care, and the integration of viral hepatitis services into existing healthcare programmes.

title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家消除病毒性肝炎的障碍以及克服这些障碍的新策略。
source_body_en: Chronic infections with hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis D virus (HDV) are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. The greatest burden is borne by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite the availability of highly effective preventive tools, simplified diagnostics, and affordable antiviral therapies, progress toward the World Health Organization's (WHO) goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030 is insufficient in most LMICs. Gaps persist throughout the entire care continuum, from vaccination and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission to screening, confirmatory testing, linkage to care, treatment initiation, and long-term follow-up. Structural weaknesses in health systems, limited laboratory infrastructure, centralised models of care, financial constraints, stigma, and fragmented disease-specific programmes continue to hinder large-scale implementation. This article examines the main barriers encountered across the viral hepatitis care cascade, from prevention and testing to treatment and long-term follow-up. It discusses practical approaches to overcoming them, including simplified diagnostic and treatment pathways, point-of-care and near-point-of-care technologies, self-testing, integrated testing platforms, decentralised care, and task sharing. Attention is given to the prevention of mother-to-child transmission, the needs of populations underserved by conventional healthcare systems, and comorbidities that influence liver disease progression. In conclusion, technological advances alone will not be sufficient. Progress will also depend on stronger health systems, decentralised models of care, and the integration of viral hepatitis services into existing healthcare programmes.
