title: Hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand
abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the difference in seroprotection between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children aged five years in northern Thailand along with the factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs in these children since vaccine implementation began in 1992. A case–control study was conducted to collect information from hill tribe and stateless individuals living in villages in Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province. Children with no prior immunization, delayed immunization, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination were included. Children who were completely vaccinated were included as controls. A questionnaire was distributed and 3 mL blood samples were collected for the qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was applied to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs. A total of 188 cases and 188 controls were included in the study; 54% were male, and 54.3% belonged to the Akha group. The overall prevalence of anti-HBs was 59.3%; 55.3% of anti-HBs was detected in children with complete vaccination (with 2 children positive for anti-HBc), and 55.3% was detected in children with incomplete vaccination. Children whose birth weight was <2500 g (AOR = 3.52; 95% CI = 1.39–9.12), whose mother belonged to the Yao group (AOR = 16.90; 95% CI = 2.00–142.57), whose mother practiced Christianity (AOR = 2.30; 95% CI = 1.18–4.46), and whose father was aged 30–39 years (AOR = 2.20; 95% CI = 1.01–4.80) were more likely to exhibit an absence of anti-HBs. The hepatitis B vaccine-induced immune response rate among hill tribe and stateless children remains undesirable, and an effective assessment program is needed to monitor this issue.

title_original: Hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of suboptimal hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity in marginalized hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand, where vaccination began in 1992. It aimed to quantify seroprotection differences between fully and partially vaccinated children and to identify factors linked to the absence of anti-HBs antibodies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case–control study was conducted in villages of Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province, enrolling hill tribe and stateless children aged five years. Cases were children with no prior, delayed, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination, while controls were those who were completely vaccinated.
analysis.methods: A questionnaire was administered and 3 mL blood samples were collected for qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was used to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs.
analysis.main_results: The overall anti-HBs prevalence was 59.3%, with 55.3% detected in both fully vaccinated and incompletely vaccinated children (2 children positive for anti-HBc among the fully vaccinated).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the low seroprotection rate as undesirable and highlighted maternal Yao ethnicity and low birth weight as strong predictors of anti-HBs absence. They concluded that an effective assessment program is needed to monitor vaccine-induced immunity in these populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings indicate that targeted vaccination programs and post-vaccination serosurveillance are warranted for hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand to improve hepatitis B immunity and reduce transmission risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported vaccination status limit causal inference and may underestimate true seroprotection gaps. The evidence is moderate due to potential selection bias and unmeasured confounders.

analysis.summary_en: This case–control study in northern Thailand evaluated hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children aged five years, comparing fully and partially vaccinated groups. Using questionnaires and blood biomarker testing, the authors found an overall anti-HBs prevalence of 59.3%, with no meaningful difference between fully and incompletely vaccinated children. Logistic regression identified low birth weight, maternal Yao ethnicity, maternal Christianity, and paternal age 30–39 years as factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs. The authors concluded that vaccine-induced immune responses remain suboptimal and called for enhanced monitoring and targeted immunization programs in these marginalized populations.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在清莱府 Mae Fah Luang 区的村庄进行了一项病例对照研究,招募了山地部落和五岁的无国籍儿童。病例是既往未接种、延迟接种或不完全接种乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 的儿童,而对照是完全接种疫苗的儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 进行问卷调查并采集 3 mL 血样用于乙型肝炎生物标志物的定性和定量检测。使用逻辑回归来检测与抗-HBs 缺失相关的因素。

source_body_en: The aim of this study was to determine the difference in seroprotection between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children aged five years in northern Thailand along with the factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs in these children since vaccine implementation began in 1992. A case–control study was conducted to collect information from hill tribe and stateless individuals living in villages in Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province. Children with no prior immunization, delayed immunization, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination were included. Children who were completely vaccinated were included as controls. A questionnaire was distributed and 3 mL blood samples were collected for the qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was applied to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs. A total of 188 cases and 188 controls were included in the study; 54% were male, and 54.3% belonged to the Akha group. The overall prevalence of anti-HBs was 59.3%; 55.3% of anti-HBs was detected in children with complete vaccination (with 2 children positive for anti-HBc), and 55.3% was detected in children with incomplete vaccination. Children whose birth weight was <2500 g (AOR = 3.52; 95% CI = 1.39–9.12), whose mother belonged to the Yao group (AOR = 16.90; 95% CI = 2.00–142.57), whose mother practiced Christianity (AOR = 2.30; 95% CI = 1.18–4.46), and whose father was aged 30–39 years (AOR = 2.20; 95% CI = 1.01–4.80) were more likely to exhibit an absence of anti-HBs. The hepatitis B vaccine-induced immune response rate among hill tribe and stateless children remains undesirable, and an effective assessment program is needed to monitor this issue.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了泰国北部边缘化山区部落和无国籍儿童因乙型肝炎 疫苗 引起的免疫力欠佳的公共卫生问题,疫苗接种 项目于 1992 年开始在泰国北部开展。该研究旨在量化完全和部分接种疫苗的儿童之间的血清保护差异,并确定与缺乏抗 HBs 抗体相关的因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在清莱府 Mae Fah Luang 区的村庄进行了一项病例对照研究,招募了山地部落和五岁的无国籍儿童。病例是既往未接种、延迟接种或不完全接种乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 的儿童,而对照是完全接种疫苗的儿童。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行问卷调查并采集 3 mL 血样用于乙型肝炎生物标志物的定性和定量检测。使用逻辑回归来检测与抗-HBs 缺失相关的因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体抗-HBs 患病率 为59.3%,在完全接种和不完全接种的儿童中检出率为55.3%(完全接种的儿童中有2 名抗-HBc 阳性)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将低血清保护率解释为不良现象,并强调孕妇的瑶族血统和低出生体重是抗 HBs 缺失的有力预测因素。他们的结论是,需要一个有效的评估计划来监测 疫苗 在这些人群中诱导的免疫力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有必要对泰国北部的山区部落和无国籍儿童进行有针对性的 疫苗接种 计划和 疫苗接种 后血清监测,以提高乙型肝炎免疫力并降低 传播 风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计和对自我报告的 疫苗接种 状态的依赖限制了因果推断,并可能低估了真正的血清保护差距。由于潜在的选择偏差和未测量的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

full_text: Abstract Background Healthcare workers and beauty service professionals are occupationally exposed to hepatitis B virus (HBV), yet comparative evidence on infection prevalence and related determinants is limited in Port Harcourt, Nigeria. This study compared the prevalence and serological profiles of hepatitis B infection between both groups and identified overall and group-specific factors associated with infection. Methods This comparative cross-sectional study was conducted in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, between August 2024 and February 2025 among 440 participants, comprising 220 healthcare workers and 220 beauty service professionals, selected using multistage sampling. Data collection employed structured interviewer-administered questionnaires and serological analysis. Blood samples were screened for HBV serological markers using the OnSite HBV-5 Rapid Test, and HBsAg-positive samples were confirmed using the BioELISA HBsAg 3.0 kit. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher’s exact tests, and logistic regression, with significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Results The prevalence of HBV infection was higher among beauty service professionals than healthcare workers (16.8% vs. 3.2%, p < 0.0001), with the highest prevalence among nail technicians (33.3%). The HBsAg/HBeAg-positive infection pattern was the most common serological profile among healthcare workers (1.8%), whereas the HBsAg/HBeAb/HBcAb-positive infection pattern predominated among beauty service professionals (12.3%). In pooled multivariable analysis, five or more sharps-related injuries in the past year (aOR: 4.86, 95% CI: 2.34–10.20; p < 0.0001) and poor HBV preventive practice (aOR: 5.93, 95% CI: 1.78–25.50; p = 0.0082) were independently associated with infection. Among healthcare workers, multivariable analysis was not feasible because of sparse infection events; however, univariable associations were observed for inconsistent PPE use, frequent sharps-related injuries, lack of occupational safety training, multiple sexual partners, tattooing, poor knowledge, negative attitude, and poor preventive practice (all p < 0.05), while among beauty service professionals, nail technician status was independently associated with infection (aOR: 4.50, 95% CI: 1.90–11.10; p = 0.0008). Conclusions Beauty service professionals had a substantially higher HBV infection burden than healthcare workers, with nail technicians predominantly affected. Frequent sharps-related injuries and poor HBV preventive practice were key predictors, highlighting the need for targeted screening, vaccination, occupational safety training, and infection-prevention interventions. Clinical trial number Not applicable. We are also grateful to the administrators and managers of the selected healthcare facilities and beauty service establishments for facilitating access to participants and supporting the conduct of the study. We further acknowledge the valuable assistance of our research assistants, Deborah Israel and Deborah Bekee, for their support with questionnaire administration and sample collection. Funding This investigator-initiated study was supported in part by a TETFund grant. The remaining aspects of the research were funded by the authors. Ethics declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate Ethical approvals were obtained from the University of Port Harcourt Research Ethics Committee (UPH/CEREMAD/REC/MM109/121), as well as from the Ethics and Research Committee of the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH/ADM/90/S.11/VOL.XI/1806) and the Rivers State Health Research Ethics Committee (RSHMB/RSHREC/2024/060). All methods employed in this study were carried out in strict accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations, including the Declaration of Helsinki and local ethical standards. Written informed consent was sought from participants after briefing them on the study’s objectives and assuring confidentiality. Participants were also informed that their participation was entirely voluntary, and they could withdraw at any point without any repercussions. Consent for publication Not applicable. full_text: J Appl Biomed X:X | DOI: 10.32725/jab.2026.008 Genetic polymorphisms in the SLC27A5 gene are associated with biochemical characteristics of HBV patients in Yunnan - Kunming University of Science and Technology, Faculty of Life Science and Technology, Kunming, China Background: Lipid droplets could influence hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication and release, as well as disease progression in patients with chronic HBV. The solute carrier family 27 member 5 (SLC27A5) gene is highly expressed in the liver and possessed bile acid-CoA ligase activity. However, no previous study has investigated the role of the SLC27A5 gene in HBV infection or disease progression. Methods: A total of 400 chronic HBV patients and 300 controls were collected in Yunnan Province to genotype three single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the SLC27A5 gene and investigate potential association between SNPs and HBV infection or biochemical characteristics of HBV patients. In silico prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assay were performed to explore the role of alleles of each SNP. Results: No association was found between HBV infection and genotypes and alleles of three SNPs (rs4801275, rs2278497, and rs56225452) in the SLC27A5 gene. However, alanine transaminase (ALT) and lymphocytes (LYM) levels differed significantly among HBV patients carrying different genotypes of rs4801275. When HBV patients were stratified into HBsAg-positive and HBsAg-negative subgroups, most hepatic functional features showed significant differences between the two subgroups. Furthermore, RNA structures containing the alleles of two SNPs were predicted, and the results indicated that different alleles could partially alter RNA structures. Dual-luciferase reporter assay also demonstrated that different alleles of the three SNPs significantly influenced firefly luciferase expression level. Conclusion: This study is the first to identify that genetic polymorphisms of the SLC27A5 gene are associated with biochemical characteristics of HBV patients in Yunnan. Furthermore, the RNA structure prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays suggest that different alleles of the three SNPs might alter the SLC27A5 gene expression levels. Keywords: Biochemical characteristics; Genetic polymorphisms; HBV patients; The SLC27A5 gene Grants and funding: This study was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (32160148). full_text_excerpt: However, no previous study has investigated the role of the SLC27A5 gene in HBV infection or disease progression. Methods: A total of 400 chronic HBV patients and 300 controls were collected in Yunnan Province to genotype three single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the SLC27A5 gene and investigate potential association between SNPs and HBV infection or biochemical characteristics of HBV patients. Results: No association was found between HBV infection and genotypes and alleles of three SNPs (rs4801275, rs2278497, and rs56225452) in the SLC27A5 gene. Furthermore, RNA structures containing the alleles of two SNPs were predicted, and the results indicated that different alleles could partially alter RNA structures. Conclusion: This study is the first to identify that genetic polymorphisms of the SLC27A5 gene are associated with biochemical characteristics of HBV patients in Yunnan. title: Hepatitis-associated virus infections in Austrian equids: a survey of equids sampled across Austria
abstract: This study aimed to determine the (sero)prevalence of equine hepacivirus (EqHV), equine parvovirus-hepatitis (EqPV-H), equid hepatitis B virus (EqHBV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV), in equids across Austria and to identify associated risk factors. In a cross-sectional study conducted between May 2023 and August 2024, 586 equids (583 horses and three donkeys) were sampled. Serum samples were analysed for EqHV RNA, EqPV-H DNA, and EqHBV DNA via qPCR/RT-qPCR and for antibodies against EqHV and EqPV-H via luciferase immunoprecipitation system. Faecal samples were tested for HEV RNA via RT-qPCR, and sera were screened for HEV antibodies via ELISA. Risk factors were assessed via multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Nucleic acid prevalence for EqHV and EqPV-H accounted each for less than 3% of the sampled animals, whereas the seroprevalence was higher: 36.9% for EqHV and 31.4% for EqPV-H. Neither EqHBV nor HEV nucleic acids were detected; one horse was HEV-seropositive. Equine hepacivirus seropositivity was significantly associated with season (spring, winter), cough and concurrent EqPV-H seropositivity. For EqPV-H, seropositivity showed significant association with younger age (1-3 years), season (winter), specific regions, EqPV-H viraemia and concurrent EqHV seropositivity. This survey confirms that EqHV and EqPV-H are endemic in Austrian equids, with low viraemia but widespread seropositivity. The absence of active EqHBV and HEV infections indicates negligible risk. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal studies to elucidate transmission pathways and investigate the clinical significance of persistent infections with EqHV and EqPV-H.
